{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 209,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Search event consumer does not handle a closed events channel",
      "body": "In searchSupport.init, the goroutine consumes events with `v := <-events` in an infinite loop. If the storage backend closes the channel (for example during shutdown), the receive returns a nil *WrittenEvent repeatedly, and handleEvent will dereference evt.Type, causing a panic. There is also no select on a context, so the goroutine cannot be stopped. Use a `for v := range events` loop or select on context/channel-ok and stop cleanly."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 762,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Resource-server watcher also reads events without handling channel closure",
      "body": "In server.initWatcher, the piping goroutine reads `v := <-events` in an infinite loop and then accesses v.ResourceVersion. If the backend closes the events channel during shutdown, this receive returns nil forever and the next field access panics. The loop should range over the channel or select on context and channel-ok."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 203,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Initial index build can permanently miss writes that happen during startup",
      "body": "searchSupport.init builds all initial indexes first and only then calls StorageBackend.WatchWriteEvents. The watch starts from the latest resource version at the time it is created, while the index snapshots were taken earlier. The resource versions returned by the builds are discarded, so writes that occur while the initial index build is running are not replayed into the index. Because startup indexing can take a long time, this can leave search results stale until another write touches the same resources. Start watching before the backfill or replay events from the build resource version."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 137,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "BuildIndex no longer serializes index creation for the same key",
      "body": "bleveBackend.BuildIndex now locks cacheMu only when assigning the completed index to the cache. Concurrent callers that see a nil index from GetIndex can therefore build the same NamespacedResource simultaneously. For file-backed indexes this can contend on the same directory, for memory indexes it creates duplicate indexes, and the final assignment can overwrite an existing index without closing it. Use a per-key mutex or singleflight so only one BuildIndex runs for a given key."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 925,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "History and Origin can nil-pointer panic when search is not configured",
      "body": "server.History and server.Origin call s.search.History and s.search.Origin without checking whether s.search is nil. NewResourceServer can leave s.search nil when search is not configured, and Search already guards for this case. A History or Origin request in that configuration will panic. Add the same nil-check used by Search."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 258,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Constructor does not clean up if Init fails",
      "body": "NewResourceServer creates a cancelable context and then calls s.Init. If Init fails after starting long-lived work, such as searchSupport.init starting its event consumer before initWatcher is attempted, the constructor returns an error without calling cancel or stopping the started components. This leaks goroutines and the cancel function. On Init failure, cancel the context and stop anything that was started."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 189,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Data race on totalBatchesIndexed and shared err during index initialization",
      "body": "In searchSupport.init, each errgroup goroutine increments totalBatchesIndexed and assigns to the outer shared err variable. With multiple worker goroutines this is a data race, and the error value can be corrupted or racy. Use a local error inside each closure and either return counts through errgroup or use an atomic counter."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 146,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "TotalDocs iterates cache without holding cacheMu",
      "body": "bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu, while BuildIndex writes to b.cache under the write lock. Concurrent map read/write in Go is a data race and can crash. TotalDocs should take cacheMu.RLock for the iteration."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Search event consumer does not handle a closed events channel
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, the goroutine consumes events with `v := <-events` in an infinite loop. If the storage backend closes the channel (for example during shutdown), the receive returns a nil *WrittenEvent repeatedly, and handleEvent will dereference evt.Type, causing a panic. There is also no select on a context, so the goroutine cannot be stopped. Use a `for v := range events` loop or select on context/channel-ok and stop cleanly.

findings.title: Resource-server watcher also reads events without handling channel closure
findings.body: In server.initWatcher, the piping goroutine reads `v := <-events` in an infinite loop and then accesses v.ResourceVersion. If the backend closes the events channel during shutdown, this receive returns nil forever and the next field access panics. The loop should range over the channel or select on context and channel-ok.

findings.title: Initial index build can permanently miss writes that happen during startup
findings.body: searchSupport.init builds all initial indexes first and only then calls StorageBackend.WatchWriteEvents. The watch starts from the latest resource version at the time it is created, while the index snapshots were taken earlier. The resource versions returned by the builds are discarded, so writes that occur while the initial index build is running are not replayed into the index. Because startup indexing can take a long time, this can leave search results stale until another write touches the same resources. Start watching before the backfill or replay events from the build resource version.

findings.title: BuildIndex no longer serializes index creation for the same key
findings.body: bleveBackend.BuildIndex now locks cacheMu only when assigning the completed index to the cache. Concurrent callers that see a nil index from GetIndex can therefore build the same NamespacedResource simultaneously. For file-backed indexes this can contend on the same directory, for memory indexes it creates duplicate indexes, and the final assignment can overwrite an existing index without closing it. Use a per-key mutex or singleflight so only one BuildIndex runs for a given key.

findings.title: History and Origin can nil-pointer panic when search is not configured
findings.body: server.History and server.Origin call s.search.History and s.search.Origin without checking whether s.search is nil. NewResourceServer can leave s.search nil when search is not configured, and Search already guards for this case. A History or Origin request in that configuration will panic. Add the same nil-check used by Search.

findings.title: Constructor does not clean up if Init fails
findings.body: NewResourceServer creates a cancelable context and then calls s.Init. If Init fails after starting long-lived work, such as searchSupport.init starting its event consumer before initWatcher is attempted, the constructor returns an error without calling cancel or stopping the started components. This leaks goroutines and the cancel function. On Init failure, cancel the context and stop anything that was started.

findings.title: Data race on totalBatchesIndexed and shared err during index initialization
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, each errgroup goroutine increments totalBatchesIndexed and assigns to the outer shared err variable. With multiple worker goroutines this is a data race, and the error value can be corrupted or racy. Use a local error inside each closure and either return counts through errgroup or use an atomic counter.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu, while BuildIndex writes to b.cache under the write lock. Concurrent map read/write in Go is a data race and can crash. TotalDocs should take cacheMu.RLock for the iteration.
